I can reproduce with [stress](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/cmd/stress) in a standalone test in go1.18 and not in go1.17:

```go
package mytest

import (
	"bytes"
	"io"
	"io/ioutil"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestSeek(t *testing.T) {
	count := 0
	testServer := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
		defer req.Body.Close()
		count++
		if count < 1000 {
			w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "1")
			http.Error(w, "Too many requests, please try again later.", http.StatusTooManyRequests)
		}
		w.Write([]byte("200"))
	}))
	defer testServer.Close()

	client := &http.Client{}

	body := bytes.NewReader([]byte(strings.Repeat("abcd", 1000)))
	req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", testServer.URL, body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for testReq(t, client, req, body) {
	}
}

func testReq(t *testing.T, client *http.Client, req *http.Request, body *bytes.Reader) (retry bool) {
	resp, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Ensure the response body is fully read and closed before we reconnect, so we reuse the TCP connection.
	defer readAndCloseResponseBody(resp)
	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests {
		body.Seek(0, 0)
		return true
	}
	// ... in non-error cases, do other things with the response body
	return false
}

func readAndCloseResponseBody(resp *http.Response) {
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	io.Copy(ioutil.Discard, resp.Body)
}
```

cc @smarterclayton ... looks like the test was added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/6671, and I'm not 100% sure our calling Seek() to reset the body of a request already sent to client.Do() is correct
reported in https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51907

Opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108981 to skip the test until the underlying issue can be resolved. This issue must remain release blocking for 1.24 until we resolve the problem, since it does not appear to be a test-only issue.

~~Looks like there is a golang regression in go1.18 (https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51907#issuecomment-1078433932)~~ (maybe not a regression... looks like @aojea could also reproduce the race in 1.17), but *also* we are not resetting the body correctly relative to draining and closing the response body. Details in https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51907#issuecomment-1077927934 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109028
@liggitt @MadhavJivrajani do we have a plan of action for this? do we call this a blocker for v1.24 release still?
Definitely release blocking. @smarterclayton is digging into the area and is on the proposed PRs
With #102217 merging, is this resolved? If not, where are we currently with respect to this blocker?

@palnabarun ~yes, that will help to a good extent and will close this out.~

Some more context (for the sake of documenting it):
- the primary source of race condition was that we weren't fully closing out the response body before reading (`Seek()`) the request body 
- this will _fully_ get resolved when the existing race condition in upstream Go (currently under investigation) gets fixed as well, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109050#issuecomment-1087577934 (we aren't blocked on the Go team here)

@palnabarun, re-read your comment, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102217 is what partially introduced the problem. 

#109050 will fix this issue.
Gotcha! Thanks @MadhavJivrajani for the context!
#109050 has merged! 🎉

> @palnabarun, re-read your comment, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102217 is what partially introduced the problem.

If I am not mistaken, #102217 preserves the original (incorrect) order as in 1.21 :
- seek to the beginning of the request body: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.21/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/request.go#L951 
- read and close response body:  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.21/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/request.go#L939-L945

In 1.24, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109050 fixes the order - close (response body) and then seek (request body).

@smarterclayton @liggitt do you think we should fix the order in 1.23, 1.22, and 1.21 as well, or does the issue manifest only with go 1.18?
It got way worse with go1.18, but I don't have a clear understanding why.
I still hit this https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/112764/pull-kubernetes-unit/1575050567246417920 in master branch.

review_comments: I don't think the comment was correct (or isn't referring to the Seek() call that follows). My understanding is that we're trying to reset the body to prep it for the retry. Discarding the body content isn't what we want
